messages.subject: Monitor resources by attribute
parts:
Hi everyone,

At our hospital, we're simulating patient flow through several resources (clinic, IC, day treatment, OR). The patients have an attribute patient_group, which determines arrival rate, length of stay, and trajectories.

Does simmer have a way to monitor the usage of the four resources by attribute? For example, I might be interested in how many patients from group 1 are using the clinic resource.

Currently, I extract arrivals and attributes, join them together, and use the code below to calculate resource usage. This works, but it's pretty slow.

Thanks in advance!
Arnoud Plantinga

# Create one row per patient per hour
ind_usage <- arrivals_attributes %>%
mutate.(time = map2.(start_time, end_time, `:`)) %>%
unnest.(time)

# Count usage
usage_counts <- ind_usage %>%
count.(replication, time, resource, patient_group,
  name = "usage"
)

On Thu, 14 Oct 2021 at 15:58, Arnoud Plantinga <arno...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi everyone,

At our hospital, we're simulating patient flow through several resources (clinic, IC, day treatment, OR). The patients have an attribute patient_group, which determines arrival rate, length of stay, and trajectories.

Does simmer have a way to monitor the usage of the four resources by attribute? For example, I might be interested in how many patients from group 1 are using the clinic resource.

# Option 1: auxiliary resources. For example:

group <- function(n) trajectory() %>%
  seize(paste0("some_resource_queue_", n)) %>%
  seize("some_resource") %>%
  release(paste0("some_resource_queue_", n)) %>%
  seize(paste0("some_resource_server_", n)) %>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, 1)) %>%
  release_all()

env <- simmer() %>%
  add_resource("some_resource", 1) %>%
  add_resource(paste0("some_resource_queue_", 1:2), Inf) %>%
  add_resource(paste0("some_resource_server_", 1:2), Inf) %>%
  add_generator("group1_", group(1), function() rexp(1, 0.2)) %>%
  add_generator("group2_", group(2), function() rexp(1, 0.3)) %>%
  run(1000)

get_mon_resources(env)

# Option 2: auxiliary globals. For example:

group <- function(n) trajectory() %>%
  set_global(paste0("some_resource_queue_", n), 1, mod="+") %>%
  seize("some_resource") %>%
  set_global(paste0("some_resource_queue_", n), -1, mod="+") %>%
  set_global(paste0("some_resource_server_", n), 1, mod="+") %>%
  timeout(function() rexp(1, 1)) %>%
  set_global(paste0("some_resource_server_", n), -1, mod="+") %>%
  release("some_resource")

env <- simmer() %>%
  add_resource("some_resource", 1) %>%
  add_generator("group1_", group(1), function() rexp(1, 0.2), mon=2) %>%
  add_generator("group2_", group(2), function() rexp(1, 0.3), mon=2) %>%
  run(1000)

get_mon_attributes(env)

---

Of course, if you are only interested in the queue or in the server, the code above can be further simplified.

Hope it helps,
Iñaki
